`parsePluginEntry` strips the `npm:` prefix and then unconditionally
prepends `clawhub:`, making the prefix a no-op. Plugins published on npm
(not ClawHub) fail with "Package not found on ClawHub" on every fresh
pod start.

Fix: pass `npm:`-prefixed entries as `npm:<spec>` to the CLI, which
already supports this resolver. Non-prefixed entries still use
`clawhub:`.

fix: sign-out no longer hangs when Supabase request stalls

The async handler used to `await supabase.auth.signOut({ scope: 'global' })`
inside try/finally. If that promise never resolved (bad network, wrong env,
unsupported scope), the function hung forever, the `finally` block never
ran, `signingOut` stayed true, the button stayed disabled, and the local
store never got cleared — even though the user clicked the button.

Now:
- Local state is cleared SYNCHRONOUSLY on click, before the network

fix(core): FormatEmu falls back to pt/inch before raw EMU

FormatEmu only tried cm before dumping a raw `<n>emu` string for any value that
didn't survive the cm round trip. But many PowerPoint/Office values are exact in
pt or inch yet NOT in cm — a 13.333in (960pt) slide width = 12192000 EMU is
33.8667cm, which the 2-decimal cm form rounds to 33.87cm and re-parses as
12193200 EMU. So slide sizes, OLE/shape dimensions, and px/pt-entered widths
read back as ugly raw EMU ("12192000emu", "609600emu"

fix feedback modal ignoring external image drag-drop on Tauri desktop because the chat webview listener intercepts all OS drops (#588)

Tauri's webview-level onDragDropEvent is global — it fires for every file
drop regardless of which UI element the cursor is over. ChatView registers
this listener on mount and never unregisters (it stays mounted with
display:none), so drops always become chat attachments. FeedbackModal only
had HTML5 onDrop, which Tauri never delivers for OS file drops.

fix(utils): guard os.fchmod for Windows in atomic_json_write

os.fchmod is Unix-only; the Windows os module has no fchmod (only
chmod). Passing mode= (e.g. 0o600 when saving the Hindsight config
during `hermes memory setup`) crashed on Windows with:

    AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'fchmod'

Guard the fchmod fast-path with hasattr(os, "fchmod"). Skipping it on
Windows is safe: mkstemp already creates the temp file as 0o600, and
the existing post-replace os.chmod(real_path, mode)
